summary.text: Matt Norris is a Democratic state representative from Minnesota House District 32B who has served since January 2023 and is seeking re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election.

An attorney, he said in a Ballotpedia survey that he is focused on lowering health care, child care and senior care costs, reforming the property tax system and increasing accountability for public spending.

paragraphs.text: Matt Norris earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Minnesota Carlson School of Management in 2011 and a law degree from the University of Minnesota Law School in 2014.
His career experience includes working as an attorney and as a policy director.

In a Ballotpedia survey, he said he grew up in the north metro area, lives in Blaine, and worked for the Step Up internship program and as policy director at a statewide youth nonprofit before being elected to the Minnesota House in 2022.
Norris assumed office on January 3, 2023, succeeding Anne Neu Brindley.
In the 2025-2026 session he was assigned to the Human Services Finance and Policy, Housing Finance and Policy, and Taxes committees, and he is co-vice chair of the Taxes Committee.
In the survey he listed among his legislative work securing $102.75 million for the Highway 65 redesign and authoring two anti-fraud bills that became law.

He said his campaign priorities include what he calls "The Three Cares" of health care, child care and senior care, property tax reform, and fraud prevention, including support for an audit of state government.
